source_row.english: Lying is when the meanings of one's spoken words are understood by the other person involved, and a wrong impression has been given him--purposely, and without any mistaken identity. Next we describe the "four expressions." 77 The Four Expressions

spans.rationale: Established lying compound; exclude is when. The words component has no separate English lexical member inside Lying.
Exact intentionality compound occurs late in English but early in Tibetan; punctuation and conjunction stay outside.
Negation belongs to the mistake condition, excluding any.
Error sense owns mistaken. Identity is explanatory specification and remains outside.

The complete noun record explicitly attests impression. This narrow mental-content noun is retained while GZHAN DU BSGYUR/wrong-given remains unbanked as a recast predicate; the noun claim does not authorize those false word atoms.
Complete speech participle has exact glossary spoken. Exclude the possessive framing.
Explicit speech noun in the meaning condition, distinct from the earlier lying compound.
Genitive links meanings to the spoken words and owns this of. The bound source genitive after SMRAS PA is not separately mapped.
Meaning/content sense owns meanings, preserving the plural translation and excluding the article.
Whole agentive-inflected OTHER PERSON compound is preserved. The agentive s cannot be separated; by/the/involved are not included inside the noun claim.
Direct glossary understood; exclude are. MNGON PAR adds an explicitness qualification but has no unique English word here.

omissions.reason: Topic, adverbial, connective and explicitness grammar is distributed into the English definition. No separate exponent or absence is proved; leave it unbanked.

Changing the perception to something else is recast as a wrong impression given. GZHAN is other, and BSGYUR is turn/change; neither alone is a secure wrong/given word pair. Keep only the independently supported impression noun.
